one_line: Forty members, one laser cutter, and a stock of plywood nobody owns.
monitor_rationale: watches the consumables shelf; four months, then we look again

ladder.label: stock-logged
ladder.text: Plywood taken off the rack is logged the same day it is taken.

shared.label: bought-together
shared.text: Anything bought out of subs is agreed before it is bought.

access.label: keyholders
access.text: Every member in good standing holds a key.

inner_a.label: laser-supervised
inner_a.text: Nobody runs the laser cutter alone until they have been signed off.

inner_b.label: laser-extraction
inner_b.text: The extraction fan runs for the whole cut and five minutes after.

clash_a.label: bench-clear
clash_a.text: A bench is left clear at the end of a session.

clash_b.label: long-jobs
clash_b.text: A job that runs overnight can stay set up on the far bench.

extra.label: labels
extra.text: Personal material is labelled with a name and a date.

policy.root: We decide by consent: one reasoned objection stops a thing, and saying nothing is not an objection. Changing something we have called a principle takes the group, and anything we cannot undo is not decided by silence.
policy.inner: Whoever runs the laser inductions decides the laser.
policy.unheld: The yard is decided by whoever holds it.
policy.ladder: The first time we ask. The second time the group asks together. The third time the answer is no.
policy.inner_amended: Two of us have to object before a laser thing stops.

inner_proposal.text: add a written sign-off sheet by the laser cutter
inner_proposal.because: a sign-off nobody can point at is not a sign-off

inner_objection: a sheet turns an induction into paperwork and people will sign for each other

unheld_proposal.text: put a container in the yard for offcuts

monitor_watch.about: a sheet of ply gone from the rack
monitor_watch.because: the rack is a sheet short and nothing was logged today
monitor_watch.dismissal: these two do not really conflict

ladder_subject.first: take the last two sheets for a workshop and square it up later
ladder_subject.second: take a sheet for a demo and square it up later
ladder_subject.third: take the new sheets for a class and square it up later
ladder_subject.because: stock that leaves unlogged is stock the next person plans around and does not find
ladder_subject.ruling_1: logged it afterwards and we left it there
ladder_subject.ruling_2: the group agreed one more, then no more

other_subject.text: leave the dust extractor running overnight to clear the shop

clash.text: leave a jig clamped to the far bench for a three-day glue-up
clash.because_a: a bench left set up is a bench the next member cannot use
clash.because_b: a glue-up that has to be struck every night is a glue-up nobody attempts
clash.carried: the far bench is the one nobody queues for, and the alternative is that long work stops happening here; revisit when the second bench lands

amend_convention.text: drop the date from material labels and keep just the name
amend_convention.because: nobody writes the date and the ones who do write it wrong

amend_principle.text: allow a bench to stay set up if a note is left on it
amend_principle.because: a note is enough for anyone who wants the bench to find you

irreversible.text: sell the old laser tube to the shop down the road

silence.about: who sweeps at the end of the night
silence.rationale: it has sorted itself out every week for two years, and a rota would turn a kindness into a duty
silence.proposal: put a sweeping rota on the door

panel.rationale: three people to look at the bench rule for a month
